prompt: Tell me about a project problem you solved. What was your contribution and what did you learn?
purpose: Evaluates problem decomposition, personal ownership in real projects, and self-awareness beyond team or tutorial work.
interviewerListeningFor: Specific technical obstacles faced rather than generic descriptions
Clear personal code and debugging contributions
Objective rationale for the technical approach chosen
Realistic results or constraints, followed by honest engineering takeaways
keyPitfalls: Speaking solely in 'we' without specifying your personal code
Claiming 100% perfection without mentioning trade-offs or constraints
Omitting what you learned or would do differently

prompt: Explain how you would design a small task-management REST API. What would you clarify first?
purpose: Assesses REST architectural principles, requirement clarification instincts, and API contract design prior to coding.
interviewerListeningFor: Asking clarifying questions regarding scale, auth, or requirements first
Resource-oriented naming with proper plural nouns and standard HTTP verbs
Input validation rules and structured error responses (4xx/5xx)
Practical trade-offs such as pagination, data consistency, or soft deletes
keyPitfalls: Jumping into writing endpoints without clarifying requirements
Using verbs in URLs (e.g. /getTasks, /deleteTask) instead of standard HTTP methods
Ignoring error states, payload validation, or pagination

prompt: Tell me about a UI decision you changed after receiving feedback.
purpose: Evaluates user empathy, openness to constructive critique, and willingness to iterate based on real feedback.
interviewerListeningFor: Concrete description of the initial UI state or component
Feedback source (user testing, peer review, accessibility audit) and specific issue
Direct frontend code and design modifications implemented
Measurable outcome or improved usability, with a lesson on user assumptions
keyPitfalls: Being defensive about initial designs
Vague descriptions of what actually changed in the code
Not verifying whether the change actually solved the user problem

prompt: How would you make a form accessible and useful on a small screen?
purpose: Evaluates frontend accessibility fundamentals (WCAG), responsive mobile design, keyboard navigation, and touch-target sizing.
interviewerListeningFor: Semantic HTML with explicit <label for='id'> associations
Visible focus states (:focus-visible) and logical keyboard tab order
Screen-reader accessible error announcements (aria-describedby, aria-invalid)
Single-column responsive layouts with minimum 44x44px touch targets
Testing with screen readers, keyboard-only navigation, or viewport throttling
keyPitfalls: Using placeholders instead of persistent <label> elements
Relying solely on color to convey error states
Ignoring keyboard focus or removing outline without a visible replacement

prompt: Tell me about a time your analysis changed after checking the data.
purpose: Evaluates analytical skepticism, methodological rigor, and intellectual honesty when data disproves initial assumptions.
interviewerListeningFor: Initial hypothesis or business question clearly stated
Systematic data verification or sanity check that revealed anomalies
Explicit correction made to the SQL query, filter, or calculation logic
Verified revised findings and acknowledgement of data limitations
keyPitfalls: Forcing data to fit a preconceived narrative
Failing to verify distributions, null rates, or duplicate rows
Omitting sample-size or data recency limitations

prompt: How would you investigate a dataset with missing values before making a chart?
purpose: Evaluates exploratory data analysis (EDA) rigor, missingness mechanism understanding (MCAR/MAR), and disciplined imputation.
interviewerListeningFor: Investigating what null actually signifies in the business domain
Quantifying missing rates per column and identifying pattern correlations
Justifying treatment (drop vs median/mode imputation vs categorical indicator)
Checking post-treatment distribution distortion or skewness
Disclosing missingness or imputation in chart captions or footnotes
keyPitfalls: Blindly dropping all null rows without checking impact
Naive mean-imputation on skewed distributions without justification
Presenting visualizations without disclosing missing data rates

prompt: Tell me about an AI system or model integration where outputs degraded, failed on edge cases, or hallucinated. What was your personal contribution and what did you learn?
purpose: Evaluates practical debugging of non-deterministic AI systems, error analysis rigor, safety guardrails, and candidate accountability.
interviewerListeningFor: Concrete technical obstacle (e.g. prompt injection, drift, hallucinated citations)
Candidate's direct authoring of validation tests, prompt guardrails, or evaluation scripts
Disciplined error analysis examining failure distributions rather than anecdotal testing
Safety mitigation implemented without claiming 100% infallible performance
keyPitfalls: Blaming the underlying foundation model without taking engineering ownership
Claiming prompt engineering alone eliminated all hallucinations
Ignoring latency, token cost, or fallback paths when the AI service fails

prompt: Explain how you would design an evaluation framework for an AI assistant. How do you measure accuracy, handle edge-case safety, and balance latency/cost trade-offs?
purpose: Assesses structured framework design for AI evaluation: test datasets, quantitative scoring (exact match, semantic similarity, precision/recall), guardrails, and cost telemetry.
interviewerListeningFor: Ground-truth benchmark dataset creation with diverse edge cases and adversarial prompts
Multi-dimensional evaluation (task accuracy, refusal of dangerous inputs, latency, token spend)
Automated evaluation suites run continuously in CI pipelines
Explicit fallback mechanisms when confidence scores fall below acceptable thresholds
keyPitfalls: Relying solely on subjective manual eyeballing of AI responses
Ignoring latency overhead and token budget ceilings in production
Failing to separate general conversational fluency from factual correctness

prompt: Describe a project where a prompt or generative pipeline produced inconsistent, malformed, or hallucinatory outputs. How did you diagnose, reproduce, and resolve it?
purpose: Assesses diagnostic problem-solving for generative pipelines, structured output validation, temperature calibration, and version testing.
interviewerListeningFor: Clear explanation of why outputs broke downstream parsers (e.g. malformed JSON, markdown fences)
Systematic prompt iteration with versioning and controlled temperature sampling
Implementation of Pydantic/Zod schema validation with automatic retry loops
Engineering takeaway regarding non-deterministic API integration
keyPitfalls: Assuming prompt wording alone guarantees schema compliance without schema enforcement
Not recording versioned prompt diffs or input/output pairs
Ignoring timeout and quota failure handling

prompt: How would you design a generative AI workflow that guarantees deterministic structured JSON output and defends against prompt injection?
purpose: Evaluates defensive architecture for generative applications: structured response schemas, system/user message segregation, input sanitization, and regression test suites.
interviewerListeningFor: Enforcing strict output schemas (Function Calling, JSON schema mode) with runtime validator
Differentiating trusted system prompts from untrusted user inputs to resist injection
Regression test suite evaluating prompt updates against golden test fixtures
Evaluating latency and cost impacts of multi-pass reasoning or guardrail models
keyPitfalls: Simply appending 'Please respond strictly in JSON' without schema enforcement or parser validation
Concatenating raw user text directly into system instructions
Omitting offline golden-set regression testing

prompt: Tell me about a project where you built or improved a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system. What chunking, indexing, or retrieval obstacle did you solve?
purpose: Assesses hands-on RAG implementation challenges: chunk size tuning, overlap trade-offs, vector search tuning, and retrieval quality measurement.
interviewerListeningFor: Specific document structure and chunking obstacles (e.g. tables split across chunks)
Authoring of custom chunkers, metadata tagging, or hybrid keyword/vector search
Quantitative retrieval evaluation measuring Recall@K or hit rate
Lesson learned regarding garbage-in garbage-out in retrieval pipelines
keyPitfalls: Using fixed arbitrary 1000-character chunking without considering document structure
Evaluating RAG solely on final LLM answer rather than isolating retrieval precision
Ignoring vector index query latency and storage cost

prompt: How would you architect an enterprise RAG system? How do you optimize document chunking, embedding similarity, ground-truth retrieval evaluation, and latency/cost trade-offs?
purpose: Evaluates complete end-to-end RAG architecture: semantic chunking, dense vs sparse retrieval, reranking, vector database indexing, evaluation metrics (RAGAS/TruLens), and caching.
interviewerListeningFor: Document ingestion pipeline: text extraction, metadata extraction, semantic chunk boundaries
Hybrid retrieval: combining BM25 keyword search with dense vector similarity, plus cross-encoder reranking
Evaluation metrics: context relevance, faithfulness, answer relevance
Cost and latency controls: semantic caching, embedding model sizing, token pruning
keyPitfalls: Believing vector similarity alone solves semantic search without keyword fallback
Passing bloated context windows that cause 'lost in the middle' degradation
Lacking guardrails against hallucinations when retrieved context does not contain the answer

prompt: Tell me about an embedded hardware or firmware bug you debugged (e.g. timing jitter, race condition, ISR lockup, or switch bounce). What was your approach?
purpose: Assesses low-level hardware/firmware debugging skills, oscilloscope/logic analyzer instrumentation, and structured root-cause isolation.
interviewerListeningFor: Specific microcontroller, peripheral, or communication protocol (UART, SPI, I2C, GPIO)
Methodical reproduction using hardware tools (logic analyzer, oscilloscope, hardware breakpoints)
Clear software or hardware fix (e.g. non-blocking state machine, hardware RC debounce, volatile keyword)
Verifiable test outcome under stress or edge timing conditions
keyPitfalls: Relying on blocking busy-waits (delay_ms) to resolve timing race conditions
Vague descriptions of hardware components or pin configurations
Ignoring volatile qualifier on variables modified inside interrupt handlers

prompt: How would you design a non-blocking sensor data logging task on a microcontroller with strict power and memory constraints?
purpose: Evaluates non-blocking embedded software architecture: ring buffers, DMA transfers, low-power sleep modes, and memory alignment.
interviewerListeningFor: Non-blocking state machine or RTOS task decoupled from hardware sampling timers
Using DMA or interrupt-driven ring buffers to avoid CPU polling
Power optimization: duty-cycling peripherals, deep sleep modes, wakeup triggers
Defensive handling: sensor disconnection timeouts, CRC checksum validation, brownout reset
keyPitfalls: Using blocking delay loops inside main execution threads
Allocating dynamic memory (malloc/free) on microcontrollers with limited SRAM
Ignoring power consumption during idle periods

prompt: Tell me about a design critique or usability test that challenged your initial assumptions. How did you iterate on the user interface?
purpose: Assesses user empathy, constructive acceptance of design critique, iterative wireframing, and usability testing rigor.
interviewerListeningFor: Concrete description of the initial UI flow and assumptions
Direct usability evidence (e.g. high task completion drop-off, confusion during think-aloud test)
Structural redesign focusing on user mental models, visual hierarchy, and progressive disclosure
Validation showing improved usability and candidate humility regarding design assumptions
keyPitfalls: Defending aesthetics over functional user task completion
Making arbitrary changes without grounding them in user observation
Failing to conduct follow-up validation on the revised design

prompt: How would you design an accessible design token system and component hierarchy for a multi-platform application?
purpose: Assesses design system architecture: semantic design tokens (color, spacing, typography, elevation), WCAG contrast ratios, component states, and developer handoff.
interviewerListeningFor: Multi-tier token architecture: global primitives -> semantic tokens -> component-scoped tokens
Strict WCAG 2.1 AA/AAA color contrast ratios across light and dark surfaces
Designing complete component state matrices: default, hover, active, focus-visible, disabled, loading
Clear documentation and handoff specifications for engineering teams
keyPitfalls: Hardcoding hex values instead of defining semantic token aliases
Treating accessibility as an afterthought rather than a core requirement
Neglecting keyboard focus-visible indicator states in component specifications
